tsdecrypt, vendored source
==========================

Upstream:  https://github.com/gfto/tsdecrypt
License:   GNU GPL v2 (see tsdecrypt/COPYING)

Pinned commits, fetched 2026-09-29:

tsdecrypt    f4876e84cf1866645f84b93f830af67193c85f69
libfuncs     55d6236c87e8920563b89af6cd1bf276b423a9a7
libtsfuncs   1482ed310186c4fecec2e409e1125316c51cf9c5

Why this is vendored instead of cloned at install time
------------------------------------------------------

tsdecrypt keeps libfuncs and libtsfuncs as git submodules, and its
.gitmodules points them at the author's own server:

    url = https://georgi.unixsol.org/git/gfto/libtsfuncs.git
    url = https://georgi.unixsol.org/git/gfto/libfuncs.git

So the documented "git clone && git submodule update --init" only works while
that host is up. It is one person's box, not a mirror network, and when it is
unreachable the clone succeeds with two EMPTY directories and the build fails
much later with a confusing missing-header error. Both libraries are also
published on GitHub, which is what this copy uses.

Vendoring the three trees means a tuner node builds from what the release
already put on disk, with no network access at all.

Not a binary
------------

The source is shipped, not a compiled tsdecrypt, and that is deliberate.
FFdecsa_init benchmarks the CPU at build time to pick the fastest descrambling
variant (usually PARALLEL_128_SSE2), so the result is specific to the machine
that compiled it. A prebuilt binary would either be slower everywhere or crash
with an illegal instruction on an older CPU.

Updating
--------

    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/gfto/tsdecrypt.git
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/gfto/libfuncs.git
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/gfto/libtsfuncs.git
    rm -rf tsdecrypt/libfuncs tsdecrypt/libtsfuncs
    cp -a libfuncs tsdecrypt/libfuncs
    cp -a libtsfuncs tsdecrypt/libtsfuncs
    find tsdecrypt -name .git -prune -exec rm -rf {} +

then replace vendor/tsdecrypt with the result and update the commits above.
